## 1. Thrift Item Matching via Donor-Price-Condition Tripartite Graphs: Recovering Hidden Categories When Condition Labels Are Noisy Proxies

`thrift_store_pricing` × `matching_recommendation` · non_obvious · generated 2026-09-07 · **Unreviewed**

Identifier: `2026-09-07_thrift-tripartite-matching-noisy-condition`

**Question.** Use bipartite graph matching on a synthetic thrift inventory to recover latent item categories when condition text is deliberately corrupted, forcing the matcher to infer affinity from price structure alone and revealing whether market-meaningful clusters survive noisy feature collapse.

**Model's assessment.** The seam is real: standard matching assumes clean node attributes (condition labels), but thrift pricing *does* encode category membership through price clustering even when condition descriptions are unreliable OCR/freeform text. The technique adaptation—using price quantile matching as a fallback when condition similarity fails—forces a genuine methodological choice about feature reliability.
